rationale: Emergency Medical (section 7) does not pay for pre-existing conditions, and the hospital records show that within the 60 days before the policy was bought on 20 June 2026 he saw his urologist on 14 May 2026 about left flank pain with blood in the urine, had a CT showing a 5 mm stone in the left kidney, and had his potassium citrate increased with tamsulosin added — the same stone the treating team removed in Mexico City. The policy has no Pre-Existing Condition Waiver, so the whole $6,200 is excluded; even after the $100 deductible it would only have come to $6,100 within the $25,000 maximum, but the exclusion means nothing is payable.
